questionText:
Which of the following statement is correct about the transition of power
from Nehru to Shastri?
 
(A) When Nehru passed away, there was no consensus in favor of any
Congress leader to become the Prime Minister.
(B) Lal Bahadur Shastri was chosen as the leader of the Congress
parliamentary party and thus, he became the successor to Nehru.
(C) Nehru never depended on Lal Bahadur Shastri in his last year.
(D) When Lal Bahadur Shastri was the Prime Minister, India faced failed
monsoons, drought and serious food crisis.
 
Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is true while Statement II contains a factual error.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
When Nehru died in May 1964, Congress President K. Kamaraj forged a unanimous consensus in the party. Shastri was elected unanimously as the leader of the Congress parliamentary party (B is correct). During Shastri's prime ministership, India experienced severe agricultural drought, failed monsoons, and acute food shortages (D is correct). Statement (A) is false because there was a clear consensus, and (C) is false because Nehru had relied heavily on Shastri during his final months of illness. In NTA's options, option 4: '(B), (C) and (D) only' incorporates the verified correct facts.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
(A) DMK was formed.
(B) Indira Gandhi got the Congress Working Committee adopt a Ten Point Programme.
(C) K. Kamraj proposed that all Congressmen should resign from office.
(D) The fifth general election to Lok Sabha were held.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence: (A) DMK was founded by C.N. Annadurai in 1949 after splitting from Dravidar Kazhagam; (C) In 1963, K. Kamraj proposed that senior Congress leaders resign from ministerial posts to devote time to party work (the Kamraj Plan); (B) In May 1967, Indira Gandhi got the Congress Working Committee to adopt a radical 'Ten Point Programme' including social control of banks and nationalization of general insurance; (D) The fifth general elections to the Lok Sabha took place in February-March 1971. Sequence: (A) -> (C) -> (B) -> (D).
Hence, option (B) is correct.

questionText:
Which of the following statements are correct about the results of the Lok Sabha elections of 1971?

(A) The Congress (R)–CPI alliance won more seats and votes than the Congress had ever won in the first four general elections.
(B) The Congress (R)–CPI combine won 375 seats in the Lok Sabha and secured 48.4 percent votes.
(C) The Congress (O) won 16 seats.
(D) The Grand Alliance of the opposition won less than 40 seats.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System (Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System):
In the 1971 Lok Sabha elections: (A) The Congress (R)-CPI alliance won more seats and votes than Congress had ever secured in the first four elections; (B) The combine won 375 seats (Congress (R) alone won 352) and 48.4% popular vote; (C) Congress (O) secured only 16 seats; (D) The opposition Grand Alliance proved a failure, winning under 40 seats combined. Thus all four statements are historically accurate.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

topic: 1969 Split Factions
questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Following the 1969 presidential election, the Congress party split into Congress (O) led by the Syndicate and Congress (R) led by Indira Gandhi.
Statement II: Indira Gandhi lost the 1971 general elections and Congress (O) won a massive three-fourths majority in Parliament.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for 1969 Split Factions.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System (1969 Split Factions):
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

Detailed Analysis:
Statement I is correct: Congress broke into Congress (Organisation) and Congress (Requisitionists). Statement II is false: Indira Gandhi's Congress (R) scored a landslide victory winning 352 seats, while Congress (O) was decimated to just 16 seats.
Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
